content: Hydroquinone, octinoxate, and oxybenzone are depigmenting agents approved by the FDA for the treatment of hyperpigmented skin conditions such as chloasma, melasma, and freckles. Common adverse reactions include hypersensitivity. Indications and Dosage for Adults: ALPHAQUIN® HP 4% Cream is indicated for the gradual bleaching of hyperpigmented skin conditions, including chloasma, melasma, freckles, senile lentigines, and other areas of melanin hyperpigmentation. The cream should be applied to the affected areas twice daily, in the morning and before bedtime, or as directed by a physician. Unnecessary solar exposure should be avoided. There is no recommended dosage for children under 12 years of age unless advised and supervised by a physician. The container should be kept tightly closed. Slight darkening of the cream is normal and does not affect its potency. Off-Label Use and Dosage for Adults: There is limited information regarding off-label guideline-supported or non-guideline-supported use of hydroquinone, octinoxate, and oxybenzone in adult patients. Pediatric Indications and Dosage: There is limited information regarding FDA-labeled or off-label use of hydroquinone, octinoxate, and oxybenzone in pediatric patients. Contraindications: ALPHAQUIN® HP 4% Cream is contraindicated in individuals with hypersensitivity to hydroquinone or any of the other ingredients. The safety of topical hydroquinone during pregnancy or in children under 12 years of age has not been established. Warnings: Hydroquinone is a skin-bleaching agent that may produce undesired effects if not used as directed. Physicians should be familiar with the contents of the product insert before prescribing or dispensing this medication. To assess potential irritation or sensitivity, patients should initially apply the medication to a small area of unbroken skin near the pigmented area for several days. Minor redness is not necessarily a contraindication, but treatment should be discontinued if itching, excessive inflammation, or vesicle formation occurs. Close patient supervision is recommended. Use in paranasal and infraorbital areas increases the likelihood of irritation. If no improvement is observed after two months of treatment, the product should be discontinued. Sunscreen use is essential during hydroquinone therapy, as even minimal sunlight exposure stimulates melanocyte activity. The sunscreens in ALPHAQUIN® HP 4% Cream provide necessary sun protection during skin-bleaching activity. During maintenance therapy following intensive depigmentation, sun exposure of the bleached skin should be avoided to prevent repigmentation. The product contains sodium metabisulfite, a sulfite that may cause allergic-type reactions, including anaphylactic symptoms and life-threatening or less severe asthmatic episodes in susceptible individuals. Sulfite sensitivity is more common in asthmatic individuals than in non-asthmatics. Keep this and all other medications out of the reach of children. In case of accidental ingestion, contact a physician or poison control center immediately. Avoid contact with eyes. If accidental contact occurs, rinse eyes thoroughly with water and contact a physician. A bitter taste and antiseptic effect may occur if applied to the lips. Adverse Reactions: No systemic adverse reactions have been reported. Occasional hypersensitivity (localized contact dermatitis) may occur, in which case the medication should be discontinued, and the physician notified immediately. Postmarketing Experience: There is limited information regarding postmarketing experience with hydroquinone, octinoxate, and oxybenzone. Drug Interactions: There is limited information regarding drug interactions with hydroquinone, octinoxate, and oxybenzone. Use in Specific Populations: Pregnancy: Hydroquinone is classified as Pregnancy Category C. Animal reproduction studies have not been conducted, and it is not known whether hydroquinone can cause fetal harm or affect reproductive capacity. The degree of systemic absorption of topical hydroquinone is also unknown. It should only be used in pregnant women when clearly indicated. Labor and Delivery: There is no FDA guidance on the use of hydroquinone, octinoxate, and oxybenzone during labor and delivery. Nursing Mothers: It is not known whether topical hydroquinone is absorbed or excreted in human milk. Caution is advised when used by nursing mothers. Pediatric Use: Safety and effectiveness in children below the age of 12 years have not been established. Geriatric Use: There is no FDA guidance on the use of hydroquinone, octinoxate, and oxybenzone in geriatric patients. Gender, Race, Renal Impairment, Hepatic Impairment, and Immunocompromised Patients: There is no FDA guidance on the use of hydroquinone, octinoxate, and oxybenzone in these specific populations. Administration and Monitoring: Administration is topical. There is limited information regarding monitoring of hydroquinone, octinoxate, and oxybenzone. Overdosage: No systemic reactions have been reported from the use of topical hydroquinone. However, treatment should be limited to relatively small areas of the body at one time, as some patients may experience transient skin reddening and a mild burning sensation, which does not preclude treatment. Pharmacology: There is limited information regarding the pharmacology, pharmacodynamics, and pharmacokinetics of hydroquinone, octinoxate, and oxybenzone. Nonclinical Toxicology: There is limited information regarding nonclinical toxicology. Clinical Studies: There is limited information regarding clinical studies. Storage: Store at 20°C to 25°C (68°F to 77°F), with excursions permitted between 15°C and 30°C (59°F and 86°F). Brief exposure to temperatures up to 40°C (104°F) may be tolerated, provided the mean kinetic temperature does not exceed 25°C (77°F). Protect from freezing. If freezing occurs, warm to room temperature. Precautions with Alcohol: The interaction between alcohol and hydroquinone, octinoxate, and oxybenzone has not been established. Consult your doctor about the effects of alcohol with this medication. Brand Names: ALPHAQUIN® HP Look-Alike Drug Names: There is limited information regarding look-alike drug names.
